title_en: Two-Track Safety-Gated Inference for Risk-Control Decision Support
abstract_en_180w: We present a two-track safety-gated inference architecture for risk-control operations over meaning-rich cross-reference signals. The system separates K-track (knowledge/research lane) from T-track (operational survivorship and rollback lane) to prevent direct promotion of overfit signals into operations. Claims are artifact-anchored and reproducible through multi-baseline comparison, raw OOS readiness checks, bootstrap/permutation significance, and falsification boundary scans. Current as-of artifacts indicate bundle readiness and publication-claim readiness under tested conditions; significance supports positive delta, and falsification reports first non-pass at survivor threshold 7. A fail-boundary layer sets max-safe survivor floor at 5 and first-break at 7 for explicit no-go semantics. Historical corpora are treated as stress-test beds for context-filter robustness, not doctrinal proof. The system prioritizes risk-off governance, auditability, and reproducibility over directional market claims.
contributions_en: Two-track architecture that separates K-track research insight generation from T-track operational gating.
Falsification-first validation with explicit fail-boundary and rollback semantics.
Public-safe disclosure strategy with as-of artifact reproducibility for applied review.
